item.title: Caring for Museum Objects
item.description: Practise the words museum teams use to handle, label and display objects. Learn to describe an object's condition and explain how to protect it.

children.definition: Work done to repair a damaged object and bring it closer to its earlier appearance.
children.example: During the restoration of the painted screen, the team reattached broken fragments to recover the outline of the original design.

children.definition: Likely to break or be damaged easily.
children.example: The handle of the glass jug was too fragile to bear its weight.

children.definition: A copy made to look as much like the original object as possible.
children.example: Visitors could turn the handle of a working replica of the clock.

children.definition: A written record of the physical state of an object at a particular time, including any damage.
children.example: The condition report noted a small crack near the base of the bowl.

children.definition: A support that holds an object in place while it is on display.
children.example: A custom mount held the shell at an angle so visitors could see its underside.

children.definition: A container with clear sides that protects objects while allowing people to see them.
children.example: The team locked the display case after arranging the coins.

children.definition: A small sign next to an object that identifies it or tells visitors about it.
children.example: The object label beside the jacket explained who had worn it and on what occasion.
children.translation_ru: табличка с названием или описанием экспоната
children.translation_uz: eksponat nomi yoki u haqdagi maʼlumot yozilgan lavhacha

children.definition: To touch, hold or move something gently so that it is not damaged.
children.example: The packing note says to handle with care because the mirror has a loose corner.
children.translation_uz: buyumni ehtiyotlab ushlamoq yoki joyidan siljitmoq
collocations: handle with care at all times

children.definition: Soft material placed around or beneath something to protect it from knocks or pressure.
children.example: We put extra padding under the sculpture before closing the crate.

children.definition: The amount of moisture in the air.
children.example: The technician checked the humidity inside the case before putting the wooden mask on display.

children.definition: For metal to become dull or change colour as it reacts with substances in the surrounding air.
children.example: The silver clasp had begun to tarnish around the edges.
children.translation_ru: тускнеть или менять цвет в результате реакции металла с веществами в воздухе
children.translation_uz: havodagi moddalar taʼsirida metall sirti xiralashmoq yoki uning rangi oʻzgarmoq

children.definition: A unique code a museum assigns to an item it formally adds to its permanent collection.
children.example: The registrar used the accession number to link a photograph of the bowl to its entry in the museum database.
children.translation_uz: muzey fondiga qabul qilingan buyumning inventar raqami

children.definition: A small amount of a substance that remains on a surface after something has been removed or has dried.
children.example: The old tape left a sticky residue on the back of the frame.

children.definition: Bright light that makes it difficult to see, especially when it reflects off a surface.
children.example: We moved the spotlight to reduce the glare on the glass in front of the drawing.
children.translation_ru: слепящий свет, в том числе отражённый
